docs.title: Core Assembly
docs.text: View Materials List

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Core is well, the core of the blaster. It is the main mechanism that stores and releases energy to power the movement of the dart, using the barrel as a guide. It is fully removable for easy swapping, maintenance and touch of flair. The Core defines the action (either bolt action or straight pull), the handedness, as well as the power by way of the spring selection. For max performance, the core is also ideally tuned to the barrel (see Tuning/Maintenance for more details). Above is an example of a right side bolt action core.

  • Plunger Sub Assembly
  • Final Assembly

docs.title: Steps
docs.text: No documented steps in the reference document for this section.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Slide the Catch onto the PrimeBlock Assembly as shown, until it is just in front of the CatchLever. Make sure the orientation of the Catch is correct, with the pointy side facing down and the larger side facing towards the PrimeBlock.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Rotate the Catch Lever down, and insert a 0.625" Long Compression Spring into the bottom of the PrimeBlock as shown. Rotate the Catch Lever back up, trapping the spring into the circular indent on its top, then slide the Catch under the Catch Lever to lock it in place.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Attach the Catch to the Pump Bars using (2) 6-32 ⅛” Socket Head Screws screwed through (2) CatchBearings. Loctite is highly recommended.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Note: the CatchBearings are considered a semi-consumable part. They can wear out over time, especially if they are detached and reattached.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Warning: Installing the PlungerAssembly upside-down can cause the core to jam closed. Pay careful attention to alignment.

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: Line up the Plunger Assembly with the PrimeBlock Assembly, making sure the angle of the CatchEnd aligns with the face of the Catch. Slide the Plunger Assembly into the CatchEnd, then secure with (2) 6-32 ⅛” Socket Head Screw

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: The Plunger Sub-Assembly is the half of the core that stores energy and is released upon firing, pushing air down the plunger tube to propel the dart. It slides inside the plunger tube and along the barrel, and is the assembly with the most impact on the performance and efficiency of the blaster.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Take the PlungerHead, CatchEnd, and SpringBase (first photo, second photo, third photo respectively) and clean out their respective center through holes (closeup of PlungerHead center section in fourth photo). These inner sections will slide on the Barrel/CatchTube, and so minimizing friction is key for performance and consistency. Remove any stray plastic, and sand out any inconsistencies if needed. If desired, you can lightly sand the inside with some fine sandpaper, though be sure not to fully sand out the ridges as these are key to minimizing friction and clearing out debris.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Test fit to make sure the PlungerHead and CatchEnd slide freely on the Barrel, and the SpringBase slides freely on the CatchTube (bottom photos). If they do not slide freely, sand out the inside until they slide with minimal resistance. Note: PlungerHead has an o-ring that it primarily slides on, so the inner ridges should be a looser fit. CatchEnd and SpringBase will directly slide on these ridges, so they should be able to slide freely but not be overly loose. See tuning notes for more in depth information about optimization and fitment.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Take the CatchTube and insert either end (it is symmetric) into the PlungerHead (first photo). It should be a relatively snug fit. Carefully rotate it until the holes align, it may take some effort due to the snug fit (second photo), then confirm that all four holes line up well. If these do not align, the PlungerHead may not be able to attach well to the CatchTube, and a new CatchTube may be needed. Then, rotate the CatchTube again until the holes are hidden (this is to provide a base for the heat set insert in the next step, and to prevent molten plastic from getting into the CatchTube holes).

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Carefully install (4) 6-32 ¼” Heat Set Inserts into the four PlungerTube holes (first photo), pushing until the insert is up against the CatchTube (cutaway in second photo). Once the heat set inserts cool, confirm the CatchTube rotates, and confirm its holes now align with the heat set inserts (third photo). Remove and set aside the CatchTube. Place a 127 O-Ring around the PlungerHead, and an 016 O-Ring inside (fourth photo). Take another 127 O-Ring, and thread it back and forth across the front cutouts of the PlungerHead to act as a bumper (fifth photo).

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: Note: If using the optional TPU Bumper use this instead of the second 127 O-Ring.

docs.title: Step 7
docs.text: WARNING: Incorrectly installing the screws in this step can permanently damage the CatchTube, which may require replacing. Be very careful to only thread the screws into the holes of the CatchTube, and do not overtighten which may strip the threading.

docs.title: Step 8
docs.text: Insert the CatchEnd onto the CatchTube, being careful to align the holes (first photo). Carefully screw in (4) 6-32 ⅛” Socket Head Screws into the four holes (second photo), tightening until flush and secure (third photo). Loctite is recommended. Confirm the CatchEnd still slides freely over the Barrel (fourth photo). If it does not, check to make sure the screws are correctly threaded into the CatchTube (otherwise they may just be pushing against the CatchTube compressing it without securely fastening). If the screws are correctly threaded and it is still too tight to slide freely, lightly sand out the inside of the CatchEnd until the Barrel can slide freely without being overly loose.

docs.title: Step 9
docs.text: Slide the SpringBase onto the CatchTube, making sure the flat diagonal side with the rectangular holes is facing the CatchEnd and the side with the rounded recess is facing out (first photo). Rotate the SpringBase until its angled face aligns with the angled face of the CatchEnd (second photo).

docs.title: Step 10
docs.text: Slide the Spring onto the CatchTube (first photo), making sure the base of the spring fits cleanly into the groove of the SpringBase (second photo).

docs.title: Step 11
docs.text: Warning: Incorrectly installing the screws in this step can permanently damage the CatchTube, which may require replacing. Be very careful to only thread the screws into the holes of the CatchTube, and do not overtighten which may strip the threading. The heat set inserts in the PlungerHead help prevent overtightening and allow repeated removal/installation, though still be careful as missing the holes can dent the CatchTube.

docs.title: Step 12
docs.text: Place the PlungerHead on the end of the CatchTube, making sure to push it on as far as it will go and rotating until the holes align (top photo). Carefully screw in (4) 6-32 ⅝” Phillips Screws, tightening until secure without overtightening (top right photo). Loctite is recommended. I also recommend first loosely installing a single screw, and confirming the remaining holes still align before tightening and installing the remaining screws. Make sure the screws are installed far enough that they are below the 127 O-Ring to prevent scraping in the plunger tube (bottom left photo). Confirm the SpringBase can move freely along the CatchTube, compressing the Spring (bottom right photo).

docs.title: Step 13
docs.text: Apply some Lube to the inner 016 O-Ring of the PlungerHead (first photo), then confirm the entire assembly moves freely on the Barrel (second photo).

docs.title: Step 14
docs.text: Note: It may take a little sliding and rotating before the lube disperses enough along the barrel to move easily. If the PlungerHead is too tight, it may indicate the screws missed the holes and are instead compressing the CatchTube without proper fastening. If after checking the screws the problem persists, you can remove the inner 016 O-Ring, check the inside of the PlungerHead, and sand down the inside until the barrel slides freely. Alternatively, you may need to adjust for printer tolerances of the inner 016 O-Ring groove to allow for smoother movement

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
BABP is designed to be modular with multiple customization options. Above are 3 example builds with their associated options.

BABP supports multiple front shroud options. See Shroud Assembly for options and assembly instructions.

Additionally, BABP supports both bolt action (a rotation at the start/end of the prime sequence to unlock/lock the breach in the closed position) and straight pull priming. It does this through a modular set of Receiver, MidBody, and PrimeBlock. Not all are compatible with each other however, and the following table shows what combinations work. First select which PrimeBlock you want (determining the action), then select a compatible Receiver and finally MidBody.

*Technically works but not recommended, as putting a straight pull in a bolt action midbody results in an unused and misleading cutout

docs.text: No documented steps in the reference document for this section.

docs.title: Final Assembly
docs.text: View Materials List

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: You are almost there! All that's left is putting the final pieces together and you will have a working blaster.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Insert both BodyBars into the StockAssembly with the circular notch facing up. Slide them in fully, making sure the notch aligns with the hold through the side of the StockAssembly, then insert a Quick-Release Pin to lock them in place.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Remove the TransferBarAdapter from the TransferBar and set it aside. Slide the TransferBar through the rectangular cutout on the backside of the Turnaround until the Pusher is sealed snugly into the back of the Turnaround.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Slide the Turnaround, PlungerTube, and TransferBar Assembly onto the BodyBars. Make sure the nubs on the Stock line up with the cutouts on the back of the Turnaround, then slide the assembly on fully until the Turnaround is flush with the Stock.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Slide on the TubeSpacer, making sure the cutout is facing backwards towards the Magwell. Slide it on fully until it is flush with the Turnaround.

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: Slide on the TubeHolder, making sure the TubeHolderInsert is facing away from the PlungerTube and the TubeHolder slides over the PlungerTube locking it in place. Reattach the TransferBarAdapter, again making sure the side with the cutout faces down.

docs.title: Step 7
docs.text: Slide on the ReceiverAssembly until flush with the TubeHolder.

docs.title: Step 8
docs.text: Apply some Lube to the outer 127 O-Rings of the PlungerHead, the inner 016 O-Ring, as well as the inside of the CatchEnd.

docs.title: Step 9
docs.text: Slide the Core into the PlungerTube through the Receiver. Slide the Core all the way back, making sure the raised section on the back of the PrimeBlock clicks in behind the front section of the TransferBar Adapter. The PlungerHead should slide easily within the PlungerTube. If it does not, make sure to distribute the lube within the PlungerTube, applying more lube if necessary.

docs.title: Step 10
docs.text: Slide on the MidBody of your choice. Make sure the dowels in the Receiver, as well as the nubs on both the middle of the Receiver and the top of the MidBody, line up and slot in cleanly. Slide the MidBody until flush with the Receiver, rotating the Handle out of the way if necessary.

docs.title: Step 11
docs.text: Apply some Lube in a ring around the Barrel around 1in/2.5cm from the back edge, then insert the Barrel through the PrimeBlock all the way down the blaster until seated fully inside the Turnaround. You should feel a distinct thunk as the barrel seats inside the 016 O-Ring within the Turnaround.

docs.title: Step 12
docs.text: Slide the GearTensionerAssembly onto the front of the blaster until flush with the MidBody.

docs.title: Step 13
docs.text: Turn the OuterGear until the hole in the TensionerBlock lines up with the notch in the BodyBars, then insert a Quick-Release Pin to secure it in place. Hand tighten the OuterGear to tension the blaster until the body is stiff and the OuterGear can no longer be turned by hand. Especially when using PLA or plastics that are susceptible to creep, it is advisable to de-tension the blaster when not in use.

docs.title: Step 14
docs.text: Again making sure the Barrel is pushed back fully in place and seated as far as it will go within the Turnaround, tighten the Thumbscrew in the Gear Tensioner Assembly to lock the Barrel in place. You can use the hex socket to tighten the Thumbscrew to further secure the Barrel in place, as the LockBlocks within the Gear Tensioner will prevent the metal portion of the Thumbscrew from making contact with the Barrel. Still, be careful not to significantly overtighten to avoid crushing the barrel.

docs.title: Step 15
docs.text: If using the optional SCAR, insert two 016 O-Rings into the grooves in the backside of the SCAR. Then push it firmly onto the front of the Barrel until the SCAR snaps into place, with the Barrel seated firmly within both 016 O-Rings.

docs.title: Step 16
docs.text: [TODO animation of firing sequence]

docs.title: Step 17
docs.text: The blaster is complete! Insert a standard talon compatible magazine, then prime the blaster by pulling the Handle back (rotating if necessary for bolt action variants) until the Catch clicks and the Plunger Sub Assembly is locked in the compressed position, then push the Handle back into the forward position to load a dart. Aiming the blaster in a safe direction, pull the Trigger to shoot a dart! Enjoy!

docs.title: Gear Tensioner Assembly
docs.text: View Materials List

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: FrontConnectorCap (1), FrontConnectorBase, Your chosen Shroud (Railgun style here)

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: LockBlockCap, TensionerBlock, 2x LockBlock, NutCap, BarrelGear, 2x SideGear, OuterGear, InnerGear

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: 2x 3/4th in 3/32” dowel, 2x 10-32 nut, 1x 3-32 by 6mm heat set insert, 1x washer, 2x 6-32 nut, 1x 1-1/4th in Oval Head Screw, 2x 5/8in 6-32 socket head bolt, 4x 6-32 5/16th screw, 2x 6-32 thumbscrews.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Warning: This section requires glueing, read the entire instruction before starting as you will have limited time to complete before the superglue sets.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Insert the 1 1/4th in 10-32 screw into the InnerGear on the circular side (first photo). Screw on the 10-32 nut until it fits into the cutout on the bottom of the InnerGear, leaving the screw slightly out (first and second photo). Apply a small drop of super glue to the underside of the screw head and top of its threads, then quickly screw it in until it is fully against the InnerGear and the nut on the other side is snug (third photo). Wipe off any excess glue, then allow 15 minutes to dry.

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: Place FrontConnectorCap on top of your chosen Shroud (first photo). Attach the two with 2x 5/16th screws in the inner two bottom holes, then apply some lube to the bottom where the gears will rest (second photo). Insert the BarrelGear, large side down in the top compartment (third photo). Insert two SideGear into their respective side cutout, small side down, with a 3/4th inch dowel in each (fourth photo). Place the OuterGear in the outer cutout as well (fourth photo). Finally, place the InnerGear with its glued in screw in the bottom cutout, then place the washer on top (fifth photo).

docs.title: Step 7
docs.text: Take the TensionerBlock and insert a 10-32 nut in the compartment (first photo). Take the NutCap and insert the split flanged side first until it clicks into the grooves on the left and right above the nut (second and third photo). Test that the pin fits easily through the hole across the entire block, then remove (fourth photo).

docs.title: Step 8
docs.text: Take the FrontConnectorBase and insert a 6-32 heat set into the top hole within the rectangular block (first and second photo). Push in as straight as possible until flush with a soldering iron set to the appropriate temperature for your print (third photo), then trim any excess (fourth photo).

docs.title: Step 9
docs.text: In this step we will be placing the FrontConnectorBase on top of the FrontConnectorCap assembly. There are a number of pieces that must fit together, so make sure you understand everything that must align before pushing the piece into place. The left and right dowels fit into corresponding holes(first photo, red and green arrows). The InnerGear’s screw goes through the larger center hole (first photo blue arrow). Finally make sure the top left and top right grooves align (second photo). Push FrontConnectorBase snugly into place once you verify all the alignments (third photo).

docs.title: Step 10
docs.text: Screw the Shroud into the heat set insert in FrontConnectorBase with a 5/16th screw from the top (first photo). Use two 5/8th socket head bolts to screw FrontConnectorCap into FrontConnectorBase from the shroud side, being careful not to overtighten (second photo blue arrows). Next, flip the assembly back over and insert two 6-32 nuts into the little slots on the left and right of FrontConnectorBase (third photo red arrows). Additionally, insert both LockBlocks into their grooves, with the tapered side down (third photo green arrows). Place the LockBlockCap on top into the fitting cutout, and use a 5/16th screw to screw it into place (fourth photo).

docs.title: Step 11
docs.text: Place the TensionerBlock into the bottom of the assembly with the smaller side face up, making sure it aligns with the cutout behind (first photo). Additionally, take two 6-32 thumb screws and insert them into the holes on the top left and right of the assembly until they screw into the captive nuts above the LockBlocks (first and second photo blue arrows). Turn the OuterGear on the side to pull the TensionerBlock into place until the hole aligns with the cutout (second photo red arrow). The bolt should be roughly flush with the end of the TensionerBlock (third photo). Finally, test that the inserted thumbscrews when tightened push the LockBlocks into the center where the barrel will ultimately go, locking the barrel into place (fourth photo green arrows). Back off the thumbscrews to allow a barrel to be inserted later.

docs.title: Loader Assembly
docs.text: View Materials List

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: The Loader Assembly is responsible for loading a dart and sealing it within the barrel/turnaround. It is moved by the core during the prime cycle.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Install a 1/4"-20 3/8" Screw through a 202 O-Ring into the front of the Pusher. Tighten until the O-Ring seals when inserted into the back of the Turnaround without being overly tight. This seals behind the dart, and so an airtight seal is important for the overall performance of a blaster. Being overly tight however will make priming the blaster less smooth, so the trick is finding the balance between the two. Note that bolt action cores lock the Loader Assembly in place and so can get away with a looser seal. Straight pull cores require a tight enough seal that the assembly doesn’t get blown out when fired. See Tuning/Maintenance for more info on tuning the seal.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Test that the TransferBarAdapter fits on the front of the TransferBar. It should slide into the cutout and be flush with the sides of the TransferBar. This piece will need to be removed and reattached when assembling/disassembling the blaster, so make sure the piece fits in smoothly, sanding/adjusting print tolerances if needed.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Install the Pusher onto the TransferBar, making sure it is aligned as shown above using (2) 6-32 ⅝” Socket Head Screw. The Pusher needs to be on the same side of the TransferBarAdapter that has the center cutout, as this is what will be in contact with the PrimeBlock.

docs.title: Prime Block Assembly
docs.text: View Materials List

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
There are 5 distinct priming blocks, depending on which action and side you prefer. They all share some common assembly, described below, as well as some specific assembly by prime block variant.

  • Common Assembly
  • Bolt Action Assembly
  • Straight Pull Assembly
  • Dual Straight Pull Assembly

docs.title: Steps
docs.text: No documented steps in the reference document for this section.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text: No documented steps in the reference document for this section.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: On the front side of the PrimeBlock, attach (2) 623 POM Bearings using (2) 8mm M3 Socket Head Screws inserted through the top. Be careful to make sure the screw goes through the center of the bearing and does not crush the bearing due to misalignment. Best practice is to insert a bearing, hold it in place with your finger, make sure the center holes align, then hand tighten the screw while being careful the bearing does not move out of position. Do not overtighten and strip the cut plastic threads, but just enough so the screw is fully inserted and the bearing is secure.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: On the rear of the PrimeBlock, attach (2) 623 POM Bearings using (2) 8mm M3 Socket Head Screws. As these bearings are farther in, it can be easier to insert them with the PrimeBlock upside-down. Again be careful to not crush the bearing , and do not overtighten.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Rotate the PrimeBlock upside-down then insert the Barrel through the center. Place a single 623 POM Bearing in the center slot.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Using the Barrel as reference, identify the bearing positioning that best fits given your printer tolerances and barrel sizing. The Barrel should slide easily without being too loose. Once you have determined the ideal positioning, secure the bearing with a single 8mm M3 Socket Head Screw.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Take the PumpBars, and line them up with the back of the PrimeBlock. Make sure the side with the farther spaced holes faces the PrimeBlock (top photo). Then, slide them into the PrimeBlock until flush with the front (bottom photo) and make sure the holes align. The bars may be a tight fit, and may need gentle encouragement with a mallet or hammer.

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: Take the CatchLever, and line it up with the bottom rear of the PrimeBlock. Slide it into the cutout, and make sure the hole aligns.

docs.title: Step 7
docs.text: Insert a single 3/32in by ¾ in Dowel through the side of the PrimeBlock, securing the CatchLever in place. This may require some hammering or pushing in with pliers. Once the dowel is inserted and flush, make sure the CatchLever is able to rotate freely.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: On the front of the PrimeBlock, insert a 6-32 Hex Nut into the cutout on the inside and screw in a 6-32 ⁵⁄₁₆” Phillips Screw from the outside to secure it, making sure it goes through the Pump Bar. Repeat on the other side on the front of the PrimeBlock.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: On the back of the PrimeBlock, insert a 6-32 Hex Nut into the cutout on the inside and screw in a 6-32 ⁵⁄₁₆” Phillips Screw from the outside to secure it, making sure it goes through the Pump Bar. Repeat on the other side on the back of the PrimeBlock.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Insert a reinforcing 6-32 ⅝” Socket Head Screw into the top back on each side of the PrimeBlock. Make sure it is fully inserted, but do not overtighten.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Insert (2) reinforcing 6-32 2" Phillips Head Screw into each handle. Make sure it is fully inserted, but do not overtighten.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Slide (2) HandleHead of your choice onto each handle on the PrimeBlock, making sure the attachment hole is facing down. Use a 6-32 ⅛” Socket Head Screw to secure it to the handle, again making sure not to overtighten.

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: On the bottom of the PrimeBlock, attach a 623 POM Bearing with an 8mm M3 Socket Head Screw, making sure the bearing is securely in place without overtightening. Repeat on the other side.

docs.title: Receiver Assembly
docs.text: View Materials List

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Take an 8mm PTFE Tube and insert it into the pivot hole of the Trigger (first and second photos). If it does not fit in you may need to file out the hole and/or adjust printer tolerances. Confirm that a 3/32in by ¾ in Dowel fits through the inserted tube and can rotate freely (third photo), then remove the 3/32in by ¾ in Dowel and set it aside. Repeat the same for the Sear (third to sixth photos).

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Insert the Trigger into the bottom of the Receiver (first photo), making sure the holes align (second photo). Press a 3/32in by ¾ in Dowel into the receiver and through the Trigger (third photo), then press the dowel all the way through until it is securely in both sides of the Receiver (fourth photo). Make sure the Trigger rotates freely.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Using the above animation as reference, install a 0.625" Long Compression Spring behind the trigger and the Sear with a 3/32in by ¾ in Dowel. First, move the Trigger forward and install the 0.625" Long Compression Spring in the circular cutout in the Receiver. Pull the Trigger all the way back so that the Sear can be moved into place so the teeth engage. Once the Sear has been positioned and the hole aligns with the Receiver, push a 3/32in by ¾ in Dowel into place and let the Trigger relax into its resting position.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Slide the Grip onto the back of the Receiver (first photo). Screw it in place with (2) 6-32 ⅝” Phillips Screws (second photo).

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Install a 3/32in by ¾ in Dowel in the top slot on the front of the Receiver (first photo). Slide it in as far as it will go (second photo). If the dowel does not fit, you can carefully bore out the slot with a 3/32 drill bit. The dowel is meant to stay attached to the Receiver, so if it does stay as a friction fit, you can use a drop of superglue to secure it in place. If you are using the ReceiverDualWindow variant, there will be an additional symmetric dowel on the other side (third photo).

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: Take the TriggerGuard and install the handle side first in the Receiver (second photo), then bend the front side in until it slots into place in front of the Sear (third photo).

docs.title: Shroud Assembly
docs.text: View Materials List

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The shroud has two variants documented in the reference guide:

  • Railgun Variant

  • Railgun Bipod Variant

  • Bipod Sub Assembly

docs.title: Steps
docs.text: No documented steps in the reference document for this section.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Insert the RightLeg into the right side of the Core, then secure it with a 6-32 ⅝“ Socket Head Screw. Make sure the indent in the RightLeg faces inwards, otherwise you may have put it on the wrong side.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Insert the LeftLeg on the left side of the Core, and secure it with a 6-32 ⅝“ Socket Head Screw. Again confirm the indents in both Legs face inward.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Optionally sand/file the front angled section of RightLockNub and LeftLockNub smooth (first photo), this will help make the locking assembly smoother and shorten the breaking in process. Then take RightLockNub and LeftLockNub and place them in Cap, nub side facing into the Cap. Finally, compress and place a Spring in the center between RightLockNub and LeftLockNub.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Take the Cap and LockNubs and place it on the bottom of the Core. Secure it with a 6-32 ⁵⁄₁₆” Phillips Screw on the back of the Cap. Confirm the LockNubs can move freely, and spring back to the outside position when released.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Optionally, sand or file smooth the inner center edges of the Button (first photo), as these will slide against RightLockNub and LeftLockNub. Then take (2) 3/32 in by ¾ in Dowels and insert them into the left and right holes in the Button.

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: Insert the Button into the front of the Core, making sure the top guides align and the Dowels enter into the Cap. Verify that pushing the Button retracts the left and right LockNub. This will likely be sticky at first, but repeated use should break in the Button until it is smooth and the Spring is able to return the Button to the unpressed position.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Install a 6-32 ¼” Heat Set Insert into RGB_Insert, making sure it sits flush and does not protrude. Insert the RGB_Insert flat side up into the RGB_MainBody, pushing it in as far as it will go.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Insert the longer RGB_TopSupportBar and the shorter RGB_BottomSupportBar into the respective slots in the rear of RGB_MainBody. Depending on print tolerances, they may require gentle encouragement with a hammer. Make sure they are inserted fully. Then screw in a 6-32 ⁵⁄₁₆” Phillips Screw into the bottom of RGB_MainBody to lock RGB_Insert and RGB_BottomSupportBar into place.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Install RGB_Base to RGB_MainBody, making sure the support bars seat correctly within the base then secure with (5) 6-32 ⅝“ Socket Head Screws, being careful not to overtighten.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Slide in Bipod Sub Assembly into the front of RGB_MainBody, making sure the Legs slot into the grooves and are flush with the sides. Then, use a 6-32 ⅝“ Socket Head Screw to connect the Bipod Sub Assembly to the RGB_Insert in its Heat Set Insert. Make sure it goes through the Button locking it in place, and is not installed too tightly such that the Bipod can swivel in the next step. Loctite is recommended.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Confirm the Legs can be pulled out with a bit of force to overcome the soft lock, and that the LockNubs extend behind the Legs when fully extended hard locking them into place. Confirm the Bipod can then swivel side to side, which may require loosening the 6-32 ⅝“ Socket Head Screw installed in the last step. To close the Bipod, press the Button on the front to retract the LockNubs so the Legs can be returned to their closed position.

docs.title: Stock/Magwell Assembly
docs.text: View Materials List

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Note: This step is optional. The StockButt can be used as is without StockButtBackplate. When printing StockButt out of a soft filament, e.g. TPU, however the StockButtBackplate can be useful to add rigidity and prevent the StockButt from peeling off the Stock and to have a more secure attachment point.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Apply a thin bead of super glue around the groove on the back side of StockButt (first photo). Take the StockButtBackplate and line it up with StockButt, making sure the holes align (second photo). Press the two pieces together, ensuring the ridge on StockButtBackplate fits into the groove in StockButt and the glue makes solid contact (third photo). Set aside for 15 minutes for the glue to set, clamping or weighting down to maintain full contact if needed.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Insert ReleaseNub into the backside of Stock, making sure the angled front side is facing down (first photo). Insert the 0.625" Long Compression Spring into the hole on the backside of ReleaseNub (second photo). Take the StockButt (and StockButtSpacer if using) and line it up with the back of the Stock, using (2) 6-32 ⅝” Phillips Screws to secure it in place (third photo).

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Take the Release and line it up with the Magwell, making sure the larger side is facing down (first photo). Spreading open the split side, slide the Release over the front of the Magwell until it closes back into place (second photo).

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Slide the Magwell onto the front of the Stock (first photo). Make sure the retaining shoulder aligns with the cutout (second photo), and the split side of the Release slides over the front of the ReleaseNub (third photo).

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text: Continue sliding the Magwell into Stock as far as it goes (first photo). Then, confirm that pushing the front of the Release retracts the ReleaseNub inside of the Magwell, and that the spring pushes it back out when released (second animated photo).

docs.title: Turnaround Assembly
docs.text: View Materials List

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: The Plunger Tube Assembly consists of the PlungerTube as well as the components that hold it on either end. The PlungerTube ultimately houses the Plunger Sub Assembly. Upon firing, the PlungerHead moves rapidly down the PlungerTube, moving air back and into the Turnaround which then redirects air into the Barrel behind the dart.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Apply some superglue to the angled face and top of the TubeHolderInsert, then insert it into the front side of the TubeHolder. Make sure the PlungerTube fits into the back of the TubeHolder. Remove the PlungerTube and set aside.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Install a 016 O-Ring in the groove on the inside of the Turnaround (first photo). Install a 127 O-Ring in the outer groove of the central section of the Turnaround. The bottom portion of the O-Ring may require pushing in with a screwdriver.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Clean out the PlungerTube, removing any dust or debris. Then, push it onto the front of the Turnaround over the 127 O-Ring until it is seated firmly against the back of the Turnaround. Make sure the 127 O-Ring is fully seated within the groove in the Turnaround and fully inside the PlungerTube, and that it is not buckled or pushed out of the PlungerTube. This should be a relatively tight fit and may require some finessing. Lube is optional, but used sparingly can help get the PlungerTube seated properly.
